question: By which principal deity and limbs are offerings prescribed in the eastern altar?
premises: The ritual context involves offerings made after establishing the fire of Śiva.
Śiva is designated as the principal element in the prescribed action.
The limbs accompany the principal deity in the ritual performance.
The eastern altar is specified as the location for these prescribed acts.
inference: Offerings in the eastern altar are prescribed to be performed with Śiva as the principal deity together with the limbs.
uncertainties: Whether aṅgaiḥ refers specifically to mantra-limbs or to ritual accessories is not fully explicit.
plain_english: They are prescribed to be performed with Śiva as the principal, together with the limbs, in the altar on the eastern side.
